baseline.description: Predict log1p Cu from 50 nearest retained training sites in EPSG:3005 with inverse-squared-distance weights. Break distance ties by sample ID. If fewer than 50 training sites, stop. Exact zero distance uses mean of zero-distance training targets. Fixed k=50 transferred from earlier US soil work; no tuning on BC scores.

candidates.configuration: Fit a mean log1p Cu per source rock_class with shrinkage of 20 pseudo-observations at the overall training mean: (sum_class + 20*globalMean)/(n_class+20). Unknown/unseen class uses the global training mean. Compute training residuals from those class means. Predict class mean plus the same 50-neighbor inverse-squared-distance weighted residuals. Clip predicted log1p Cu below zero to zero. No hyperparameter search.

eligibility.sourceIdentity: Verify exact bundle/survey/analytic-package links and actual workbook headers against source metadata; do not infer colon keys from packed URL IDs. Metadata adaptation may map names without changing semantics. Any unexplained bundle, method, preparation, survey or identifier mismatch stops admission.
eligibility.sampleIdentity: Run the pinned CDoGS identity selector: controls, second field duplicates, blind duplicates and competing analyses of one physical sample are excluded. Preserve source NGR/master references. Canonical lab IDs include the documented source namespace. Unknown master relationships must be resolved without target values or the run stops.
eligibility.spatialOrder: On all identity/method-eligible metadata rows, regardless of target missing/censor status, apply all-pair 100m coincidence exclusion, 100km prior evidence quarantine, fixed grid allocation and 10km partition buffers. Only then exclude missing/censored targets from the quantified regression. No magnitude thresholds, outlier removal or winsorization.
eligibility.priorEvidence: Before claiming independence bind complete non-target coordinate/identity extracts of prior BC RGS2020, USGS DS801 and Copperwood evidence, not only their audit subsets. Preserve all reported conflicting Copperwood positions. Any unlocated prior records or unresolved cross-source lineage stop until documented geographic coverage resolves exclusion; never fabricate coordinates. Geography and different hashes alone are not proof of independent provenance.
eligibility.geology: Acquire a bounded, byte-bound snapshot of intersecting bedrock polygons, object IDs and ROCK_CLASS only, explicitly in NAD83 EPSG:4269. Validate response CRS, pagination completeness, ring topology and source identity. Join source sample coordinates by polygon interior; boundary/no match/multiple matches/null class become UNKNOWN without dropping samples. Use exact trimmed class labels, no assay-driven grouping. UNKNOWN/unseen class uses global training mean. Do not use mineral occurrences, geochemical provinces, other elements, assay-derived covariates, depth or economic features.

split.group: x=6371.0088*cos(66*pi/180)*(lon+140)*pi/180 km; y=6371.0088*(lat-60)*pi/180 km. Group=floor(x/25):floor(y/25). This local equirectangular grid is approximate; it is not an equal-area projection.
split.assignment: SHA256 UTF8 yukon-eagle-plains-cdogs-cu-icpms-bedrock-v1|<gridX>:<gridY>; unsigned first 8 hex digits modulo 100; 0..59 train, 60..79 validation, 80..99 audit.
split.distance: Haversine spherical distance with radius6371.0088km, clamp haversine term to[0,1]. Coordinates remain source NAD83; no datum accuracy beyond source is claimed.
split.buffer: Remove train within strictly less than10km of initially eligible validation or audit locations; remove validation within strictly less than10km of initially eligible audit locations. Fixed reference sets; never reassign or restore exclusions. Audit unaffected by partition buffering.
split.minimums: After quantified-target exclusion each partition needs >=100 samples and >=8 distinct groups, otherwise stop without fitting or resplitting.

baseline.configuration: 50 nearest retained training sites by declared spherical distance; ties by canonical sample ID in Unicode code-point order. Inverse-squared-distance weighted natural log1p Cu. Exact zero distance uses mean of all zero-distance training targets. No tuning.

candidate.configuration: Global mean of retained training log1p Cu. Known class mean=(class target sum+20*globalMean)/(class count+20); UNKNOWN/unseen uses globalMean. Training residuals subtract those means. Predict query class mean plus baseline-identical50-neighbor inverse-squared-distance weighted residuals; clip final log prediction below0 to0. One fixed candidate, transferred from prior work without Yukon tuning.

evaluation.metric: Sample-weighted RMSE in natural log1p Cu; relative improvement=1-candidateRMSE/baselineRMSE. Also report MAE and actual sample/group counts. Zero baseline RMSE makes relative improvement undefined and cannot pass.
evaluation.uncertainty: 2000 paired audit spatial-group bootstrap replicates using NumPy2.5.3 Generator(PCG64(20261016)). Sort distinct group IDs in Unicode code-point order, draw the original number of groups uniformly with replacement, include all members with multiplicity and compute aggregate sample-weighted RMSE relative improvement. Linear2.5/97.5percentiles. Undefined replicate statistics cause an inconclusive result, never redraw. This is group-resampling uncertainty, not a location interval.
evaluation.execution: Before fitting, registry-bind actual source/normalized/geology/prior-inventory bytes, exact memberships, evaluator and commitment. Fit on train only. Bind training model, both validation predictions and both audit predictions before audit scoring. One fixed audit evaluation even when validation gate fails. No replacement audit if any attempt fails after audit start.
evaluation.gate: Candidate qualifies only if validation improvement>=0.02, audit improvement>=0.02, audit bootstrap lower bound>0 and all admission/membership checks pass. Otherwise retain spatial baseline, or record inconclusive if statistics cannot be computed. Passing does not authorize unsampled-region or economic predictions.
evaluation.budget: Exactly one baseline, one candidate and one audit. No retuning features, transformations, seed, grid, buffer, neighbors, shrinkage or threshold after commitment. Two exact assay workbooks, combined<=256MiB; bounded geology<=256MiB and<=100 paginated requests, sequential with>=1second spacing and source Retry-After honored. Stop on resource limit, denied access or challenge; no bypass. Local CPU only, two numerical threads maximum, no paid service or AI call.

limitations: Selected northern surveys are not representative of Yukon, Earth, undiscovered deposits or global copper supply.
Quantified-only eligibility excludes censored/missing observations and can bias concentration estimates.
A different assay method, sample support, area and grouping prevent direct numerical comparison with earlier BC or soil scores.

Mapped bedrock at a sample point is not catchment geology or depth; historical mapping may incorporate geological/geochemical interpretation. Separate publication does not prove statistical independence.
Spherical distances, local grid distortion, source position uncertainty, catchment overlap and long-range dependence remain.
This experiment cannot by itself demonstrate a recursively improved research-selection policy, calibrated uncertainty or economic forecast.
document.deviationPolicy: Archive this commitment unchanged. Record purely mechanical header/parser fixes with hashes and exposure chronology before any scoring. limitations: Registry events make protocol and exposure history inspectable; they are not model improvements.

New audit starts require archived source, normalized data, evaluator code, model, validation predictions and sealed audit predictions matching frozen identities and memberships. Generic file and row checks alone do not validate scientific execution.

The BC adapter reproduces source normalization, fixed training-only models and sealed predictions before a single score attempt. It applies only to its reviewed retrospective protocol; other sources require adapters. No automatic promotion or learned research policy is connected.
The hash chain detects changed events relative to its published head. A filesystem owner can rewrite local history; external published checkpoints are needed to detect full-chain replacement.

Audit reservations conservatively apply to the entire raw source release, across targets and normalization versions. Repackaging/renaming records can defeat raw-hash and ID-only overlap checks; a source-specific lineage review remains necessary. No reset or reuse operation is provided.
